newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Dominican Republic agrees to accept Peru rebels.
newsitem.headline: Dominican Republic agrees to accept Peru rebels.

text.p: The Dominican government on Friday formally agreed to grant asylum to some of the Marxist guerrillas holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Peru.
The announcement was made after President Leonel Fernandez met with Japanese Vice Foreign Minister Masahiko Komura, who flew to Santo Domingo from Cuba on Thursday.

"The government expressed its agreement to receive some of the rebels in Lima," a statement from the president's press office said. It added that the Dominican Republic wanted a peaceful resolution to the conflict.
"For this reason the government is prepared to offer its help in finding an end to this disturbing episode," it said.

Komura thanked the Dominican Republic and Cuba for agreeing to take in the Peruvian guerrillas if there was a negotiated settlement of the three-month hostage siege, but he was not very optimistic that would happen soon.
"There is still some distance between the Peruvian government and the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement," he said at a news conference. "We should not be too optimistic."
Cuba on Thursday formally accepted a Japanese request to grant asylum to the rebels. Komura met President Fidel Castro in Havana on Wednesday evening to make the request.
Komura said he offered the Dominican Republic nothing in return for taking in the some of the rebels. The Dominican statement said he invited Fernandez to make a visit to Japan.

The Lima crisis entered its 94th day on Friday with few signs of a solution, as the guerrillas insist on the release of hundreds of jailed comrades and show little interest in accepting asylum abroad.

The jungle-trained rebels stormed the residence on on Dec. 17 during a cocktail party and seized more than 500 captives. They are still holding Fujimori's brother, the Japanese ambassador and dozens of Japanese businessmen and diplomats.
